newsitem.title: GREECE: ATHLETICS-BUBKA REVEALS PURE COMPETITIVE STEEL.
newsitem.headline: ATHLETICS-BUBKA REVEALS PURE COMPETITIVE STEEL.

text.p: Sergei Bubka revealed the pure competitive steel which has made him the greatest pole vaulter in history by winning his sixth world title against all the odds on Sunday.

Coming into the competition with minimum training after the lingering after-effects of an Achilles tendon injury which ruined his Olympics last year, Bubka soared into the sky to win the gold with 6.01 metres.
"That 6.01 was one of his best jumps that I have seen," said Russian Maxim Tarasov, who had to settle for the silver.
"It's amazing to see him win six title at world championships."
The Ukrainian's performance on the final day of the sixth world championships was every bit as memorable as Carl Lewis's fourth Olympic long jump gold in Atlanta last year.
At a post-event news conference, where he was greeted with applause, Bubka said he had set his sights on a gold medal at each of the world championships.
"After Atlanta I was dead," he said. "Maybe that was the reason that I found motivation. My main secret is that I love sport. I was born for sport and I always want to be the best."
Daniel Komen, who missed selection in the Kenyan team for Atlanta, won the 5,000 metres in some style by suddenly accelerating away from the field with five laps to run.
"After seven laps I planned to get away," he said. "It was not easy but I was under a lot of pressure."

German Lars Riedel rose from his sick bed after a throat infection to win the men's discus for a fourth time and Donovan Bailey anchored the Canadian 4x100 metres relay team to the gold medal in the absence of the Americans who botched a baton change in the first round on Saturday.
The day began in merciless August heat with Abel Anton depriving fellow-Spaniard Martin Fiz of a second consecutive world marathon title.
Anton, the European 10,000 metres champion, outsprinted Fiz just before the pair entered the Panathinaikon stadium after running from Marathon to Athens.
Russian silver medallist walker Olympiada Ivanova became the second athlete to lose a medal and prize money when she tested positive for the steroid stanozolol.

Ivanova finished second in the women's 10 kms walk. Her compatriot Lyubov Tsyoma, who failed to finish her 800 metres semifinal heat, tested positive for the same drug and both now face two-year suspensions.
